title: Low Dust Mass and High Star Formation Efficiency at z > 12 from Deep ALMA Observations
question: What are the dust mass build-up, dust production and growth mechanisms, and star formation efficiency of UV-bright galaxies at z > 12 (GHZ2 and GS-z14-0)?

recipe.goal: Create ALMA dust continuum images and measure upper limits
recipe.method: Calibrate ALMA Band-6 and Band-8 data with standard ALMA pipeline in CASA 6.5.1, remove channels within ±300 km s^-1 of [O III] 88 µm and 52 µm lines, and create dirty continuum images with natural weighting without primary beam correction to measure r.m.s. noise and 3σ flux density upper limits.
assumptions: Target sources are unresolved / point-like at continuum and S/N is low enough not to require cleaning

recipe.goal: Constrain dust mass and dust temperature using radiative equilibrium model
recipe.method: Apply the Inoue et al. (2020) analytical radiative equilibrium model with clumpy dust geometry combining the magnification-corrected 3σ ALMA continuum upper limits (modified blackbody) and NIRCam UV effective radii and UV luminosities to find the intersection constraining M_dust and T_dust.
key_parameters: r_e,dust = r_e,UV (105 ± 9 pc for GHZ2, 260 ± 20 pc for GS-z14-0)
assumptions: Dust is in radiative thermal equilibrium, optically thin, with clumpy geometry, and has the same spatial extent as the UV stellar continuum (r_e,dust = r_e,UV)

recipe.goal: Derive total gas mass, ionized gas mass, and dust-to-gas ratio (D/G)
recipe.method: Compute total gas mass by subtracting magnification-corrected stellar mass from dynamical mass (M_gas = M_dyn - M_*), estimate ionized gas mass from Hbeta luminosity and electron density using Chávez et al. (2014), and combine with M_dust upper limits to constrain D/G vs. gas-phase metallicity.
key_parameters: Alternative gas fractions f_gas = M_gas / (M_gas + M_*) = 0.1, 0.5, 0.9
assumptions: Negligible dark matter contribution within galaxy centers (<= r_e); M_ion = 1.2 x 10^7 M_sun adopted as lower limit of M_gas for GS-z14-0

recipe.goal: Model dust production history from star formation histories and stellar yields
recipe.method: Parameterize non-parametric SFHs (from Bagpipes and Prospector) with an exponential profile SFR(t) ∝ exp(t/τ) and integrate SN and AGB dust yields following Valiante et al. (2009) across stellar masses 0.1-100 M_sun to compare predicted dust masses with ALMA upper limits and constrain SN reverse shock destruction and IMF.
key_parameters: Star formation start redshift z = 20 (GHZ2) and z = 30 (GS-z14-0)
Larson IMF with α = 1.35 and M_ch = 0.35 M_sun (and M_ch = 10 M_sun for top-heavy test), mass range 0.1-100 M_sun
assumptions: Exponentially rising SFH parameterization and Larson IMF

recipe.goal: Compute star formation efficiency (SFE) and compare with redshift evolution scaling relations
recipe.method: Calculate SFE = SFR / M_mol using SFRs averaged over 10 Myr and 100 Myr from non-parametric SFHs and assuming M_gas ≃ M_mol (from M_dyn - M_* and f_gas = 0.1-0.9), then compare against main-sequence and starburst galaxy samples and scaling relations.
key_parameters: SFR averaging timescales = 10 Myr and 100 Myr
assumptions: ISM gas is dominated by molecular gas (M_gas ≃ M_mol)

score_reason: The ALMA data processing is very simple (standard CASA 6.5.1 pipeline, natural-weighted dirty continuum images excluding ±300 km/s around [O III] lines, no PB correction) and all physical input parameters (Table 1) and analytical model constants (I20 parameters) are explicitly tabulated. Minor deductions are due to unreleased custom scripts for the I20 equilibrium solver and Valiante et al. (2009) yield integration.
rediscovery_reason: All three ALMA DDT project codes are public in the ALMA archive, the imaging recipe is straightforward (natural-weighted dirty map with a ±300 km/s line mask), and the main outputs are clear numeric 3-sigma continuum r.m.s. values and analytical dust mass upper limits.
